    def test_prepared_request_is_pickleable(self, httpbin):
        p = requests.Request("GET", httpbin("get")).prepare()

        # Verify PreparedRequest can be pickled and unpickled
        r = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(p))
        assert r.url == p.url
        assert r.headers == p.headers
        assert r.body == p.body

        # Verify unpickled PreparedRequest sends properly
        s = requests.Session()
        resp = s.send(r)
        assert resp.status_code == 200

    def test_prepared_request_with_file_is_pickleable(self, httpbin):
        with open(__file__, "rb") as f:
            r = requests.Request("POST", httpbin("post"), files={"file": f})
            p = r.prepare()

        # Verify PreparedRequest can be pickled and unpickled
        r = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(p))
        assert r.url == p.url
        assert r.headers == p.headers
        assert r.body == p.body

        # Verify unpickled PreparedRequest sends properly
        s = requests.Session()
        resp = s.send(r)
        assert resp.status_code == 200

    def test_prepared_request_with_hook_is_pickleable(self, httpbin):
        r = requests.Request("GET", httpbin("get"), hooks=default_hooks())

        # Verify PreparedRequest can be pickled

        assert r.url == p.url
        assert r.headers == p.headers
        assert r.body == p.body
        assert r.hooks == p.hooks

        # Verify unpickled PreparedRequest sends properly

        resp = s.send(r)

HTTPADAPTER is the built-in Requests transport adapter for HTTP and HTTPS URLs. It is mounted on URL prefixes, typically through a Requests session, to deliver requests through the underlying urllib3 transport layer. HTTPADAPTER creates and manages connection pools and urllib3 connections, supports proxy managers, applies TLS and SSL certificate verification settings, and provides standard request-related connection methods. It also manages serialization state and adapter-specific cleanup. As the default adapter for HTTP and HTTPS, HTTPADAPTER can be configured with retry behavior, including retry-enabled handling for HTTPS requests, and can be extended for custom SSL or other connection settings.
